text.title: Where this course comes from
text.subtitle: Dr. Long's weekend report review of November 22, 2026, read in a critical state.
text.body:
Dr. Long's weekly coaching check-in of Sunday, November 22, 2026: two hours on YouTube (rq3bTCXLvIk), the first on his AI coaching project and the week's options positioning, the second on the weekend report. The course is the second hour's heart, 01:12 to 01:42: chart two and chart three of the report, read live with Luis and another student in the room. He holds the session there himself: "we're only on chart three… all of the other ones are derivative of that insight" (s23).

The moment: SPY is down about 12 percent, 780 to 690, and Friday closed on a collapse. Every slope on the 3-day stack is down, the 270 has gone from rising to sideways, and the RL10, the SMA30 and the RL90 have each breached the 270's own Bollinger band in turn, so the 270 is coming back to its own long-term average with "a very thin layer of support, statistically" (s04). The metamodel has swing and long-term exposure at zero; the open door is the day trade and the one-to-three-day swing (s05). That is the critical state the course is named for: several signals arriving together, and the framework that reads them.

text.title: The argument, in seven chapters
text.subtitle: Four regression lines, the 270's own band, and the same reading on any time frame.
text.body: One: rig for heavy weather, the four lines and the breaches in order (s04, s05). Two: why four regression lines; price pulls away from the RL10, the 10, 30, 90 and 270 chase it, and the framework shows the turning points "when the 270 comes back to its own Bollinger band" (s07, s09). Three: the downside ladder read off the stack, the SMA30 peak, the bottom of the dragon, the bottom of the RL10, the fat tail, 690 and 660, and a recovery that has to fight back up the same stack (s11). Four: the nine-day as the same picture times three; each past sell-off, the kata 2 entry, the sideways warning, no support yet; the 270 on nine-day bars is a 2,500-day line, "that's what fractal means" (s13, s14). Five: the five mice on the run, who is shorting, who stepped aside, who is deciding; 600 is the bear line, COVID took three nine-day bars (s16, s17). Six: Luis brings the March 2020 report; the breach of the 270 was followed by another 25 percent, 285 to 220; the same distance today is 640 to 500, and the SuperPinch targets 610 and 471 agree (s19, s20). Seven: the definition. The framework is "an engineering specification": the 10 against the 270 is traders against buy-and-holders, "whether T is one minute or nine days"; the buy-and-holder buys in the existential moment with a 20 percent trailing stop, never from the top (s22, s23).

text.title: What the cut must keep
text.subtitle: A reading method, not a forecast; every number on screen is one he or Luis says.
text.body:
He never calls the direction: "Is it going to do this in a hurry, or that in a hurry? I don't know. I don't care, because I know how to trade this short-term volatility and my long-term money is protected until this thing resolves" (s07, and the maxim card).

Twelve of the thirteen animated pictures are drawn on frozen frames of his own charts, with the levels placed on his own price axis; the thirteenth is drawn where Luis speaks with no chart on screen. Three numbers the captions drop (550 in chapter 1, 630 and 645 in chapter 3) were confirmed by two Whisper models and are on screen as his. The political aside at 01:19:44 is out of the cut and off by default.

The hinge for the student, said once per chapter card and under every scene's head: the picture is the trade. The stack is where the market's long and short money sit; the band is the last support; the ladder is where the next bid may stand; the mice are who is buying and who is selling; the specification is why the same reading works on any time frame.
